title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
author: Ryan Lopopolo, OpenAI
claims: Use a small repository map and executable constraints for changes.
limits: One team's experience. No controlled time comparison.

title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
author: Anthropic Engineering
claims: A feature ledger and progress artifacts allowed subsequent sessions to resume work.
limits: Application-specific trials. The report describes premature completion and context loss.

title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
author: Anthropic Engineering
claims: Assess both final state and trajectory. Different graders answer different questions.
limits: A grader can fail even when the task succeeds. Check against human judgment.

title: Measuring the impact of early-2025 AI on experienced open-source developer productivity
author: Joel Becker, Nate Rush, Beth Barnes and David Rein, METR
claims: Sixteen developers took 19% longer on average with AI available on tasks in their own projects.
limits: 246 tasks in mature repositories. Limited population, tools and time period.

title: We are changing our developer productivity experiment design
author: METR
claims: Selection bias and concurrent work obscured later productivity estimates.
limits: No reliable speedup estimate for current users.

title: git-worktree
author: Git project
claims: A linked worktree can check out a separate branch from the same repository.
limits: Separate files do not isolate shared services, fixtures or ports.

title: Canarying releases
author: Google, The Site Reliability Workbook
claims: Evaluate a small release population against a control before rollout.
limits: Choice of signals, comparison group and duration depends on traffic.

title: Prompt caching in the API
author: OpenAI
claims: Reusing eligible input prefixes can lower processing time and input cost.
limits: Launch prices and model eligibility are historical. No consumer application timing claim.

title: How we built our multi-agent research system
author: Anthropic Engineering
version: Claude Research system described in June 2025
claims: Parallel search can explore independent sources. The team reported substantially higher token use.
limits: Vendor's workloads, tools and comparison conditions limit transfer.

title: Harness design for long-running application development
author: Anthropic Engineering
claims: Independent browser interaction exposed defects missed by self-evaluation.
limits: Adding a reviewer also adds work. No speed guarantee.

title: Building effective agents
author: Anthropic
claims: Choose fixed workflows, routing or dynamic agent control according to task structure.
limits: Patterns guide architecture. They provide no measured benefit for a particular project.

title: Building a C compiler with a team of parallel Claudes
author: Nicholas Carlini, Anthropic
claims: The team used a compiler and external tests as oracles. The author reported API costs just under $20,000.
limits: One unusually testable project. Historical project costs cannot price another task.
